ending_first.ending: Neo is shot dead by Agent Smith in room 303 of the Heart O' the City Hotel, but Trinity whispers that the Oracle prophesied she would fall in love with the One, and that man is Neo; she kisses him and his heart restarts. Neo awakens as the One — stops bullets in midair, sees the Matrix as cascading code, dives into and destroys Agent Smith from within — and the remaining Agents flee. Morpheus detonates the EMP, destroying the Sentinels attacking the Nebuchadnezzar. Neo makes a phone call to the Matrix promising to show people a world without rules, then rises into the sky and flies away.
ending_first.cost: Mouse, Apoc, Switch, and Dozer are dead; Cypher is dead; Morpheus was tortured and his mind nearly broken; Tank is wounded; five previous candidates for the One died before Neo. The war against the machines is not won — Neo's closing monologue promises change but does not deliver it. The story is about awakening, not victory.
ending_first.final_image: Neo hangs up a pay phone, slides on a pair of sunglasses, and rockets into the sky above the city, his long black coat billowing like a cape, flying faster than a speeding bullet.

jacket_copy: Thomas Anderson lives two lives: by day he writes software for a respectable company; by night he is Neo, one of the world's most dangerous hackers, searching for an answer he cannot name. A stranger named Trinity tells him the answer is looking for him. A man called Morpheus offers him a choice: a blue pill to forget, or a red pill to learn what the Matrix is. Neo takes the red pill and wakes up naked in a pod, his body a battery feeding machines that have enslaved the entire human race. Morpheus believes Neo is the One, prophesied to end the war and free humanity. The Oracle says he is not. When Morpheus is captured defending him, Neo must choose between his own life and the man who believed in him — and discover what he truly is.
plot_summary_short: The Matrix is a science fiction action film set across two timelines: the late twentieth century inside a computer simulation and approximately 2199 in the real world. The Matrix is a neural-interactive simulation that enslaves humanity by making each person experience a simulated life while their physical bodies are grown in pods and their bioelectricity harvested by machines. Death inside the Matrix kills the physical body, because the body cannot live without the mind. Freed humans can re-enter the simulation through hardwired phone lines and bend its rules through mental discipline. Neo, a hacker who senses something wrong with reality, is freed by a rebel named Morpheus, who believes Neo is the One — a prophesied savior who can reshape the Matrix. After training, Neo visits the Oracle, who tells him he is not the One and that Morpheus will die for him. Morpheus is captured by Agents — sentient programs that enforce the system and can inhabit anyone still hardwired to it. A crew member named Cypher betrays the team, killing four of them before being shot by a wounded survivor. Neo re-enters the Matrix with Trinity to rescue Morpheus. They storm a government building, extract him, but Neo is cornered and shot dead by Agent Smith. Trinity confesses her love — fulfilling the Oracle's prophecy that she would love the One — and Neo revives, stops bullets in midair, sees the Matrix as code, and destroys Agent Smith. The other Agents flee. Morpheus detonates an electromagnetic pulse to save the ship from Sentinels. Neo flies into the sky, promising to free humanity.
plot_summary_long:
The Matrix is a science fiction action film set across two timelines: the late twentieth century inside a computer simulation and approximately 2199 in the real, scorched world. The central conceit is that what humans experience as everyday life is the Matrix — a neural-interactive simulation generated by machines to keep humanity docile while their physical bodies are grown in pods and their bioelectricity harvested as fuel. Death inside the Matrix kills the physical body, because the body cannot live without the mind. Freed humans can re-enter the simulation through hardwired phone lines and bend its rules through mental discipline. The One is a prophesied figure who can break the Matrix's rules entirely and end the machine war.

The film opens with Trinity, a freed human, fighting her way past armed police with superhuman speed in the Heart O' the City Hotel and escaping through a ringing telephone. Agents — sentient programs in dark suits who enforce the Matrix and can inhabit the body of anyone still hardwired to the system — confirm their next target is a hacker called Neo. Neo is Thomas Anderson, a software programmer by day and a hacker by night who senses something is wrong with the world. He receives a message on his computer: "Follow the white rabbit." At a nightclub, Trinity warns him he is being watched and that the question driving him — "What is the Matrix?" — will find him. At his office, Agent Smith captures Neo, seals his mouth shut, and inserts a living tracking bug into his navel. Morpheus calls and sends Trinity to extract the bug; she drives Neo to the Hotel Lafayette to meet Morpheus, who offers a choice: a blue pill to forget everything, or a red pill to learn the truth. Neo takes the red pill.

The red pill is a trace program that disrupts Neo's carrier signal. He wakes naked and bald in a pod of gelatin among endless towers of human beings grown as crops by machines. A machine unplugs him from the power plant and flushes him into the waste system, where the hovercraft Nebuchadnezzar retrieves him. Morpheus tells him the real year is approximately 2199 and that the world he knew was the Matrix. In the Construct — a blank loading program — Morpheus shows Neo the scorched real world and explains that the Oracle prophesied the return of the One, a man who could reshape the Matrix at will. Neo's atrophied body is rebuilt. Combat skills are uploaded directly into his brain in seconds. In a sparring dojo, he fights Morpheus and learns that the Matrix's rules can be bent or broken through mental discipline. He fails a rooftop jump exercise and is told his mind makes the simulation real — death in the Matrix kills the physical body.

Morpheus explains that Agents are sentient programs that can inhabit anyone still hardwired to the system, and that every freed human who fought an Agent has died. A Sentinel — a real-world killing machine — attacks the Nebuchadnezzar; the crew survives by shutting down all power and detonating an electromagnetic pulse, the only weapon effective against machines. Cypher, a crew member who regrets taking the red pill, secretly meets Agent Smith inside the Matrix and offers to betray Morpheus in exchange for reinsertion into the Matrix as a wealthy man with no memory.

Morpheus takes Neo to see the Oracle, a guide who tells each person what they need to hear. She tells Neo he is not the One but warns that Morpheus will sacrifice his life for Neo's and that one of them will die. On the way back, Cypher's betrayal springs: the hotel's hardline is cut, the windows are bricked up, and Mouse is gunned down. Morpheus is captured while telling Trinity to get Neo out. Trinity and Neo escape through the walls and sewer. Cypher exits the Matrix first, kills Dozer and Tank with a lightning rifle, and unplugs Apoc and Switch, killing them instantly. He prepares to unplug Neo, but Tank — wounded but alive — shoots Cypher dead.

Agent Smith tortures Morpheus to extract the access codes to Zion, humanity's last underground city, and reveals his own hatred of the Matrix, calling it a prison he wants to escape. The crew plans to kill Morpheus to protect Zion, but Neo refuses, declaring he will re-enter the Matrix to rescue him; Trinity insists on joining.

Neo and Trinity storm a government building, massacring the lobby guards and flying a stolen helicopter to the executive floor, where Neo rakes the office with mounted gunfire and Morpheus breaks his restraints. Neo catches Morpheus in a midair cable rescue as the helicopter crashes. On the roof, Neo dodges bullets with superhuman speed and Trinity kills an Agent at point-blank range. At the subway station, Agent Smith ambushes Neo, who refuses to run. They fight hand to hand; Neo throws Smith in front of a train, but Smith reconstitutes and pursues him through the city. In the real world, Sentinels close on the Nebuchadnezzar, creating a race against the EMP detonation.

Neo reaches room 303 of the Heart O' the City Hotel, but Agent Smith is waiting with a gun. He shoots Neo dead. In the real world, Trinity whispers to Neo's body that the Oracle told her she would fall in love with the One, and that man is Neo; she kisses him, and his heart restarts. Neo awakens as the One — he stops the Agents' bullets in midair, sees the Matrix as cascading green code, dives into and destroys Agent Smith from within, and the remaining Agents flee. Morpheus detonates the EMP, destroying the Sentinels and saving the ship. Neo makes a phone call to the Matrix promising to show people a world without rules, then rises into the sky and flies away. The war is not over; the story is a beginning.
